newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up for short prompt material.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up for short prompt material.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges ticked up early on Thursday on shortage of prompt supplies but traded steady to slightly lower for regular material with demand said to be below normal.
Traders said high sulphur barges changed hands early at $88.50 a tonne in Rotterdam and Antwerp, or 50 cents above Wednesday's close, and offers reached as high as $89.
But later, they traded at $87.50/$88 a tonne and talk was $87.50/$88.50 by mid-day.
Traders said the higher numbers were paid for very prompt product which seemed to be in short supply.
"There's a shortage of prompt product and one major is buying higher," one trader said.
"If we have demand of 10,000 tonnes or more this afternoon it may move up $1 or $2," the trader added.
Other traders said demand continued to be below normal.
Low sulphur barges were unchanged, quietly talked in the $94/$95 region. One trader said demand may pick up next week as "some people may have to cover some short positions".
Russian high sulphur straight-run was still on offer at steady prices, with traders saying a number of cargoes were offered at two means plus $6.
"I was shown one Polish M-100 at two means plus $6 and there are also three Russian M-100s, and I assume they are at the same level," a trader with a major said.
Some good quality M-40 was also heard to be on the market, valued at a handsome three means +$4.
